dify: Start with safety, not features: Dify ships no supported backup for its database, uploaded files or vector store, so one lost volume erases every app and knowledge base. A documented backup and restore command is small work and is required for Level 2. Then make knowledge edits reversible and drafted: builders already upload and re-index documents themselves, but chunk and retrieval edits keep no history.
directus: Make data-model changes undoable. Admins already change collections, fields and relations in the Data Model screen, and the AI assistant drafts them, but no change keeps its prior state, so a wrong field change cannot be reversed in the product. That one gap is what users feel. Pair it with a supported backup, which Directus does not ship today.
discourse: Discourse is the best-governed product here for people making changes by hand: settings and text keep their old values and can be reverted. What it lacks is the product helping: no draft of a settings or text change from a request. Turning a top-voted feature topic into a drafted settings change is the move that takes it to Level 2, and the three moves together get there.
frappe: Frappe already lets system managers change forms, workflows, permissions and reports themselves, with history. The next level is the product helping: capture a change request inside Desk and draft the customisation for a person to finish. Add revert-to-version for definitions, which Version records already make possible, and the three moves reach Level 2.
hermes-agent: Give memory and persona an undo. The agent rewrites what it remembers about a user, and nothing keeps the previous version, so a bad memory edit is permanent. Skills already have a ledger with rollback; extend it to memory files. That is the change users feel; the change that reaches Level 2 is turning a request into a plan before the agent creates a skill (move 2).
librechat: One gap holds LibreChat at Level 0: tool connections (MCP servers) can be added and removed but keep no history, so a changed server or credential cannot be put back. Keep a version of each change with one-step undo, as agents and prompts already have. That alone gives it Level 1. Its agent writing skills does not count until it drafts something users rely on, such as agents or model settings.
n8n: n8n's AI already drafts workflows, which is why it leads at Level 2. Level 3 is a programme, not a step: it needs about fourteen changes. Start with what hurts users most: credentials have no history and deletion is permanent, so a wrong edit breaks every workflow that uses it. Give credentials versions and restore, as workflows already have, and extend undo to variables, data tables and settings.
openclaw: Give the assistant's memory and persona a real undo. Dreaming is on by default and rewrites what the assistant remembers, and the workspace is never committed, so a bad rewrite cannot be reversed. Commit the workspace on each change and expose restore, as skill collections already have. Level 3 is a longer programme: about fifteen changes, led by undo and tested restore.
opencode: OpenCode's own agents and commands are files the user must version in their own git; the agent generator writes outside any session, so its output cannot be reverted. Give agent and command changes a history with undo inside OpenCode. That is what Level 1 needs, and the first move alone does not reach it because undo for its own definitions (move 3) is also required.
openhands: Ship a supported backup for the automation service, and then let the agent draft automations from a request with a test run before they go live. Today automations are created from templates or chat and validated, but no backup exists and nothing turns a request into a plan. Level 2 also needs fix proposals and known capacity limits, listed below.
posthog: PostHog's AI already drafts charts, dashboards and flags, and its activity log records before-and-after values. What holds it at Level 1 is the fix loop: errors are grouped, but nothing works out their likely cause. Explaining a grouped error with the recent change behind it reaches Level 2. Then make the activity log revertible across surfaces, which is the main gap before Level 3.
